Some ignorant people said: supplication is contrary to reason in several respects:

First: He is the Knower of the unseen, who knows what is in souls and what breasts conceal. So what need do we have for supplication?

Second: if what is sought is known to occur, there is no need for supplication; and if it is known not to occur, there is no benefit in it.

Third: supplication resembles commanding and forbidding, and for a servant to do this toward his Master is a breach of etiquette.

Fourth: if what is sought through supplication is among the benefits, then the Wise does not neglect it; and if it is not among the benefits, it is not permissible to seek it.

Fifth: it has been reported that the highest station of the truthful (*siddiqin*) is contentment with the decree of Allah, exalted. This has been recommended, and supplication contradicts it, because it is a preoccupation with asking and seeking.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 20, verses 25–35 (part 3 of 7):**

Sixth: The Prophet ﷺ said, relating from Allah, Exalted is He: "Whoever is occupied with remembering Me instead of asking Me, I shall give him the best of what I give those who ask." This shows that the better course is to abandon supplication. The verses you have cited, however, require supplication to be obligatory.

Seventh: When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) abandoned supplication and was content with saying, "My knowledge of my condition is sufficient as a request," he earned great praise. This shows that the better course is to abandon supplication.

The answer to the first point is that the purpose of supplication is not to inform (Allah). Rather, it is a form of humble entreaty like other acts of humility.

The answer to the second point is that it is like saying to someone who is hungry and thirsty: if satiety is certain to occur, there is no need for eating and drinking; and if it is certain to occur, there is no benefit in it.

The answer to the third point is that although the form is that of a command, the manner of humble entreaty and submissiveness turns it away from that meaning.

The answer to the fourth point is that it may become a benefit on condition that supplication precedes it.

The answer to the fifth point is that if one supplicates to show humble entreaty and then is content with what Allah, Exalted is He, has decreed, that is the greatest of stations. This is also the answer to the remainder, once it is established that it is among the acts of worship. Furthermore, Allah, Exalted is He, commanded him to worship and to pray with a command stated in general terms, so he rightly proceeded to the most excellent of acts of worship, which is supplication.

The fourth aspect: concerning the excellence of supplication, Allah, Glorified is He, did not limit His explanation of its excellence to commanding it. Rather, He made clear in another verse that He is displeased when He is not asked. He said: ﴿Why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts became hard, and Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾ (al-An'am: 43). The Prophet (ﷺ) also said: "Let none of you say, 'O Allah, forgive me if You wish.' Rather, let him be resolute and say, 'O Allah, forgive me.'" For this reason, Musa (peace be upon him) was resolute in supplication and said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾.

The fifth aspect: concerning the excellence of supplication is the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿Your Lord has said: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾ (Ghafir: 60). In this there is a great honour for our community, because Allah favoured the Children of Israel with a great favour. He said concerning them: ﴿And that I preferred you over the worlds﴾ (al-Baqarah: 47), and He also said: ﴿And He gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds﴾ (al-Ma'idah: 20). Yet despite this great rank, they said to Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿Ask your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is﴾ (al-Baqarah: 70). And the disciples, despite their eminence in their saying: ﴿We are the helpers of Allah﴾ (Al 'Imran: 52), asked Isa (peace be upon him) to request for them a table spread with food to descend from heaven. Then Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, removed this intermediary for our community, and He addressed them directly without any intermediary, saying: ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾ (Ghafir: 60), and He said: ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty﴾ (al-Nisa': 32). For this reason, when this virtue was granted to this community, and Musa (peace be upon him) had come to know it, he said: "O Allah, make me of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ)." Therefore, he immediately raised his hands and said:

[Page 34]

﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾. Know that He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿When My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near﴾ (al-Baqarah: 186). Then He, Exalted is He, divided the servants into seven categories:

The first: the servant of protection (ʿabd al-ʿiṣmah): ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾ (al-Hijr: 42). Musa (peace be upon him) was specially singled out for an increased measure of protection: ﴿And I have chosen you for Myself﴾ (Taha: 41). Therefore he sought additional protection and said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾.

The second: the servant of purity (ʿabd al-ṣafwah): ﴿Peace upon His servants whom He has chosen﴾ (al-Naml: 59). Musa (peace be upon him) was specially singled out for an increased measure of purity: ﴿O Musa, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech﴾ (al-A'raf: 144). Therefore he desired greater purity and said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾.

The third: the servant of glad tidings (ʿabd al-bishārah): ﴿So give good tidings to My servants﴾, ﴿who listen to speech and follow the best of it﴾ (al-Zumar: 17–18). Musa (peace be upon him) was specially singled out for this: ﴿And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed﴾. Therefore he desired greater glad tidings and said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾.

The fourth: the servant of honour (ʿabd al-karamah): ﴿O My servants, no fear shall be upon you﴾ (al-Zukhruf: 68). Musa (peace be upon him) was specially singled out for this: ﴿Do not fear; indeed I am with you both﴾ (Taha: 46). Therefore he desired an increase beyond it and said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾.

The fifth: the servant of forgiveness (ʿabd al-maghfirah): ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ (al-Hijr: 49). Musa (peace be upon him) was specially singled out for this: ﴿My Lord, forgive me﴾ (Sad: 35). So He forgave him, and he desired an increase and said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾.

The sixth: the servant of service (ʿabd al-khidmah): ﴿Worship your Lord﴾ (al-Baqarah: 21). Musa (peace be upon him) was specially singled out for this: ﴿And I have chosen you for Myself﴾ (Taha: 41). Therefore he sought an increase in it and said: ﴿Expand for me my breast﴾.

The seventh: the servant of nearness (ʿabd al-qurbah): ﴿When My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near, I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me﴾ (al-Baqarah: 186). Musa (peace be upon him) was specially singled out for nearness: ﴿And We called him from the right side of the mount and brought him near as a confidant﴾ (Maryam: 52). Therefore he desired perfect nearness and said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾.

* * *

The third section: concerning His saying: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾. There are several aspects to this:

The first: when He addressed him with six things:
The first was the knowledge of tawhid: ﴿Indeed, I am Allah; there is no deity except Me﴾ (Taha: 14).
The second: He commanded him to worship and to pray: ﴿So worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance﴾ (Taha: 14).
The third: knowledge of the Hereafter: ﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming﴾ (Taha: 15).
The fourth: the wisdom of His actions in this world: ﴿And what is that in your right hand, O Musa?﴾ (Taha: 17).
The fifth: the presentation of the dazzling miracles to him: ﴿That We may show you of Our greatest signs﴾ (Taha: 23).
The sixth: His sending him to the people most disbelieving and insolent. These arduous duties became a cause of constraint, so Musa (peace be upon him) wished to compensate for this constraint with a miracle. He therefore was informed that everyone who asks Him draws near to Him, so he said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾. He wished to compensate for the constraint produced by these duties by nearness to Him, so he said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾. Or it is said that he feared the devils of mankind and jinn, so he supplicated in order to reach the station of nearness by means of supplication, and thereby become safe from the harms of the devils of jinn and mankind.

The second: the meaning is that he intended to go to Pharaoh and his people, so he wished to sever entirely the hopes of creation regarding himself. He knew that whoever calls upon his Lord, He brings him near and draws him close to Himself. At that point all desires are entirely cut off, so he said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾.

The third: existence is like light and non-existence is like darkness, and everything other than Allah, Exalted is He, is pure non-existence. "Everything is perishing except His Face" (al-Qasas: 88). Thus all of them are as if in the darkness of non-existence and the shade of the world of bodies and contingency. So he said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, so that my heart may sit in the bright light of knowledge and the seat of the expansion of the breast. One who sits in light does not see one who is sitting in darkness. Therefore, when he sat in the light of the expansion of the breast, he saw no one in existence. For this reason he followed it with His saying: ﴿And ease for me my affair﴾ (Taha: 26), for the servant in the state of absorption does not devote himself to any of the important matters.

The fourth: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, for the eye of the eye is weak. So, O my God, raise for me the sun of success until I see every thing as it truly is. This is in the sense of the saying of Muhammad (ﷺ): "Show us things as they truly are." Know that the expansion of the breast is a prerequisite for the shining of the divine lights in the heart, and listening is a prerequisite for the understanding that comes from hearing speech. Allah, Exalted is He, gave Musa (peace be upon him) the second prerequisite, which is ﴿So listen to what is revealed﴾. Therefore Musa followed that pattern and sought the other prerequisite, saying: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾. When the matter reached Muhammad (ﷺ), it was said to him: ﴿And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge﴾ (Taha: 114). Knowledge is the aim. Since Musa (peace be upon him) was like a prelude to the coming of Muhammad (ﷺ), he was given the prelude. And since Muhammad was like the aim, he was given the aim. Glorified is He; how subtle is His wisdom in everything.

The sixth: the one who supplicates has two attributes:
The first: that he be a servant of the Lord: ﴿When My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near﴾ (al-Baqarah: 186).
The second: that the Lord be his: ﴿Your Lord has said: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾ (Ghafir: 60). He attributed Himself to us and did not attribute us to Himself. The one occupied with supplication has become complete through these two aspects. So Musa (peace be upon him) wished to frolic in this garden, and said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾.

The seventh: Allah, Exalted is He, honoured Musa (peace be upon him) with His saying: ﴿And We brought him near as a confidant﴾ (Maryam: 52). It is as if Musa (peace be upon him) said: "My God, since You said, 'And We brought him near as a confidant,' I have become near to You. But I wish for Your nearness to me." He said: "O Musa, did you not hear My saying: ﴿When My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near﴾ (al-Baqarah: 186)? So occupy yourself with supplication until I become near to you." At that point he said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾.

The eighth: Musa (peace be upon him) said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, and to Muhammad (ﷺ) He said: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ (al-Sharh: 1). Then He did not leave him in this state, but said: ﴿And as a illuminating lamp﴾ (al-Ahzab: 46). Consider the difference: the expansion of the breast is that the breast becomes receptive to light, and the illuminating lamp is that which gives light. The difference between Musa (peace be upon him) and Muhammad (ﷺ) is like the difference between the receiver and the giver. Then we say: O our God, indeed our religion, which is the word "There is no deity except Allah," is light; ablution is light; prayer is light; the grave is light; Paradise is light. So by the truth of Your lights which You have given us in this world, do not deprive us of the lights of Your bounty and beneficence on the Day of Resurrection.

* * *

The fourth section: concerning His saying: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the expansion of the breast, and he said: "It is a light cast into the heart." It was said: "What is its sign?" He said: "Turning away from the abode of delusion, turning in repentance to the abode of eternity, and preparing for death before it descends." This indicates that the expansion of the breast is an expression for light: His saying: ﴿So is one whose breast Allah has expanded for Islam and who is upon a light from his Lord?﴾ (al-Zumar: 22). Know that Allah, Exalted is He, mentioned ten things and described them as light:

The first: He described His own essence as light: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾ (al-Nur: 35).
The second: the Messenger: ﴿There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book﴾ (al-Ma'idah: 15).
The third: the Qur'an: ﴿And follow the light which was sent down with him﴾ (al-A'raf: 157).
The fourth: faith: ﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾ (al-Tawbah: 32).
The fifth: the justice of Allah: ﴿And the earth shone with the light of its Lord﴾ (al-Zumar: 69).
The sixth: the brightness of the moon: ﴿And made the moon therein a light﴾ (Nuh: 16).
The seventh: the day: ﴿And made the darknesses and the light﴾ (al-An'am: 1).
The eighth: the clear proofs: ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light﴾ (al-Ma'idah: 44).
The ninth: the prophets: ﴿Light upon light﴾ (al-Nur: 35).
The tenth: knowledge: ﴿The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp﴾ (al-Nur: 35).

Having established this, we say: it is as if Musa (peace be upon him) said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾ through knowing the lights of Your majesty and Your greatness.

Second: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, by being adorned with the characteristics of Your messengers and prophets.

Third: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, by following Your revelation and complying with Your command and prohibition.

Fourth: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, by the light of faith

[Page 36]

and certainty in Your divinity.

Fifth: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, by gaining insight into the secrets of Your justice in Your decree and judgment.

Sixth: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, by moving from the light of Your sun and Your moon to the lights of the majesty of Your might, as Ibrahim (peace be upon him) did when he passed from the star, the moon, and the sun to the presence of might.

Seventh: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, from contemplating Your day and Your night to contemplating the day of Your grace and the night of Your justice.

Eighth: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, by gaining insight into the gatherings of Your signs and the bonds of Your clear proofs on Your earth and in Your heavens.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 20, verses 25–35 (part 4 of 7):

Ninth: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾ so that I may follow the examples of the earlier prophets and resemble them in submitting to the judgment of the Lord of the worlds.

Tenth: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾ by making the lamp of faith in my heart like the niche (*mishkah*) in which there is the lamp (*misbah*).

Know that expanding the breast (*sharh al-sadr*) is an expression for kindling light in the heart until the heart becomes like a lamp, and that light is like fire. It is known that whoever wants to kindle a lamp needs seven things: a flint (*zand*), a stone, tinder (*hiraq*), sulfur, a lamp-holder (*misrajah*), a wick, and oil. So the servant who seeks the light which is the expansion of the breast needs these seven things.

The first: the flint of striving (*mujahada*): ﴿And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our paths﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 69].

The second: the stone of humble supplication: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly﴾.

The third: the tinder of restraining desire: ﴿And he who forbade the soul from desire﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 40].

The fourth: the sulfur of turning back (*inabah*) to Allah: ﴿And turn back to your Lord﴾ [al-Zumar: 54], smearing the heads of those sticks with the sulfur of "repent to Allah."

The fifth: the lamp-holder of patience: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45].

The sixth: the wick of gratitude: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾ [Ibrahim: 7].

The seventh: the oil of contentment: ﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾ [al-Insan: 24], that is, be content with the decree of your Lord. When these tools are sound, do not rely on them. Rather, one should seek the goal only from His presence: ﴿Whatever mercy Allah opens for people, none can withhold it﴾ [Fatir: 2]. Then seek it with humility and submission: ﴿And voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾ [Ta-Ha: 108]. At that point, raise the hand of humble supplication and say: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾, and then you will be heard: ﴿You have been granted your request, O Musa﴾ [Ta-Ha: 36].

Then we say: this spiritual light called the expansion of the breast is better than the physical sun, for several reasons:

First: the sun is hidden by a cloud, but the sun of knowledge is not hidden by the seven heavens: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾ [Fatir: 10].

Second: the sun sets at night and returns by day. Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said: ﴿I do not love those that set﴾ [al-An'am: 76]. But the sun of knowledge does not set at night: ﴿Indeed, the rising at night is firmer in tread﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 6], and ﴿those who seek forgiveness at dawn﴾ [Al 'Imran: 17]. Rather, the most perfect spiritual robes are obtained at night: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night﴾ [al-Isra': 1].

Third: the sun perishes: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ [al-Takwir: 1], but the sun of knowledge does not perish: ﴿Peace, a word from a Lord, Most Merciful﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58].

Fourth: when the moon comes in front of the sun, the sun is eclipsed. But here is the sun of knowledge, which is the knowledge that "I testify that there is no god but Allah." No moon can stand before it, for "I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Its light has not reached the world of the limbs.

Fifth: the sun blackens faces, while knowledge whitens them: ﴿On the Day when some faces will be white and some faces will be black﴾ [Al 'Imran: 106].

Sixth: the sun burns, while knowledge saves from burning. Pass, O believer, for your light has extinguished my flame.

Seventh: the sun splits (the head with its heat), while knowledge ascends: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾ [Fatir: 10].

Eighth: the sun's benefit is in this world, while knowledge's benefit is in the hereafter: ﴿And the enduring good deeds are better﴾ [al-Kahf: 46].

Ninth: the sun in the sky is an adornment for the people of the earth, while knowledge on the earth is an adornment for the people of the heavens.

Tenth: the sun is high in its form but low in its meaning. This indicates envy combined with arrogance. The divine knowledges are low in their form but high in their meaning. This indicates humility combined with nobility.

Eleventh: the sun knows the conditions of creation, and through knowledge the heart reaches the Creator.

Twelfth: the sun falls upon both the friend and the enemy, but knowledge is not attained except by the friend. Since knowledge is described by these precious qualities, Musa rightly said: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾.

As for the subtle points (*nukat*):

The first: the sun is a lamp that Allah kindled for perishing: ﴿Everyone upon it will perish﴾ [al-Rahman: 26]. Knowledge is a lamp He kindled for permanence. He who created the sun for perishing: if Satan came near it, it would burn him: ﴿a piercing flame﴾ [al-Jinn: 9]. So how could Satan approach the knowledge that He created for permanence? ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾.

The second: Allah kindled the sun in the sky, and it removes darkness from your house although it is far from your house. He kindled the sun of knowledge in your heart. Will it not remove the darkness of disobedience and disbelief from your heart, though it is close to you?

The third: whoever kindles a lamp keeps tending it and feeding it. Allah is the One who kindles the lamp of knowledge: ﴿But Allah has endeared faith to you﴾ [al-Hujurat: 7]. Will He not feed it? This is the meaning of His words: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾.

The fourth: when a thief sees a lamp lit in a house, he does not approach it. Allah has kindled the lamp of knowledge in your heart, so how could Satan approach it? Therefore he said: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾.

The fifth: the Magians kindled a fire and do not want to extinguish it, while the King, the Holy One, kindled the lamp of faith in your heart. How would He be pleased to extinguish it? Know that He, glory be to Him and exalted, has given the heart of the believer nine honors.

The first: life: ﴿Is he who was dead and We gave him life?﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. When Musa, peace be upon him, desired spiritual life, he said: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾. Then the subtle point is that he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever revives a dead land, it is his." When the servant revives a land, it belongs to him. So when the Lord created the heart and gave it life with the light of faith, how could anyone else have a share in it? ﴿Say: Allah, then leave them﴾ [al-An'am: 91]. Just as faith is the life of the heart, disbelief is its death: ﴿Dead, not alive, and they do not perceive﴾ [al-Nahl: 21].

The second: healing: ﴿And He will heal the breasts of a believing people﴾ [al-Tawbah: 14]. When Musa desired healing, he raised his hands and said: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾. The subtle point is that when He placed healing in honey, it remained healing forever. Here, when healing is placed in the breast, how could it not remain healing forever?

The third: purity: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾ [al-Hujurat: 3]. When Musa, peace be upon him, desired attaining the purity of piety, he said: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾. The subtle point is that when a goldsmith tests gold once, he does not afterward put it into the fire. Here, when Allah has tested the heart of the believer, how would He put it into the fire a second time? But Allah does put into the fire the heart of the disbeliever: ﴿That Allah may distinguish the evil from the good﴾ [al-Anfal: 37].

The fourth: guidance: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah, He will guide his heart﴾. Musa, peace be upon him, desired additional guidance and said: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾. The subtle point is that the Messenger guides the self, the Qur'an guides the spirit, and the Master guides the heart. Since guidance from disbelief through Muhammad ﷺ sometimes occurs and sometimes does not: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Qasas: 56]. And the guidance of the spirit, since it comes from the Qur'an, sometimes occurs and sometimes does not: ﴿By it He misguides many and by it He guides many﴾ [al-Baqarah: 26]. But the guidance of the heart, since it comes from Allah, does not cease, because the Guide does not cease: ﴿And He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ [Yunus: 25].

The fifth: writing: ﴿Those, He has written faith upon their hearts﴾ [al-Mujadila: 22]. When Musa, peace be upon him, desired that writing, he said: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾. In this there are subtle points:

[Page 38]

The first: paper has no great value, yet when the Qur'an is written on it, it is not permissible to burn it. The heart of the believer has been written with all the rulings concerning the Essence of Allah, the Exalted, and His attributes. How then is it fitting for the Generous One to burn it?

The second: Bishr al-Hafi honored a sheet of paper on which the name of Allah was written, and he attained the happiness of both abodes. So honoring a heart in which is the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, is more worthy of this.

The third: a sheet of paper with no writing on it, when the Greatest Name of Allah is written on it, its status becomes so great that a person in a state of major impurity (*junub*) or a menstruating woman may not touch it. Indeed, al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: it is not permissible for him to touch even the cover of the mushaf. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 79]. So the heart in which is the most honored of creatures: ﴿And We have honored the children of Adam﴾ [al-Isra': 70], how could the wicked Satan touch it? And Allah knows best.

Sixth: tranquility (*sakinah*): ﴿It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers﴾ [al-Fath: 4]. When Musa, peace be upon him, desired tranquility, he said: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾. The subtle point is that Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and was afraid. When tranquility descended upon him, he said: ﴿Do not grieve﴾. When the tranquility of faith descended, they hoped to hear the address: ﴿Do not fear and do not grieve﴾ [Fussilat: 30]. Also, when tranquility descended, they became successors: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth﴾ [al-Nur: 55], meaning that they would become vicegerents of Allah on His earth.

Seventh: love and adornment: ﴿But Allah has endeared faith to you and made it beautiful in your hearts﴾ [al-Hujurat: 7]. The subtle point is that whoever plants a seed in the earth does not spoil it or burn it. He, glory be to Him and exalted, has planted the seed of love in the earth of the heart, so how would He burn it?

Eighth: ﴿And He joined your hearts together﴾ [Al 'Imran: 103]. The subtle point is that Muhammad ﷺ joined the hearts of his companions together, and then he did not leave them, whether absent or present: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah." So how would the Merciful leave them?

Ninth: serenity (*tuma'nina*): ﴿Surely by the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest﴾ [al-Ra'd: 28]. Musa sought serenity and said: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾. The subtle point is that the servant's need has no end. Therefore, even if he were given everything in the world of bodies, it would not suffice him, because his need is endless and bodies are finite. A finite thing cannot be equal to what is infinite. What suffices for an endless need is a perfection that has no end, and that is none but the Real, glory be to Him and exalted. Therefore He said: ﴿Surely by the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest﴾ [al-Ra'd: 28].

Since you have come to know the reality of the expansion of the breast for believers, know the characteristics of the hearts of disbelievers in several respects:

First: ﴿So when they turned aside, Allah turned their hearts aside﴾ [al-Saff: 5].

Second: ﴿Then they turned away; Allah turned their hearts away﴾ [al-Tawbah: 127].

Third: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾ [al-Baqarah: 10].

Fourth: ﴿And We made their hearts hard﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 13].

Fifth: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it﴾ [al-An'am: 25].

Sixth: ﴿Allah has sealed over their hearts﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7].

Seventh: ﴿Or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ [Muhammad: 24].

Eighth: ﴿No! Rather, rust has covered their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 14].

Ninth: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has sealed﴾ [al-Nahl: 108].

O our God and our Master, by Your grace and kindness, close these nine doors of abandonment (*khidhlan*) from us, mend us by Your kindness, and open for us those nine doors from Your kindness, by Your grace and mercy. Indeed, You are capable of whatever You will.

* * *

The Fifth Section: concerning the reality of the expansion of the breast. The scholars have mentioned two aspects regarding it:

[Page 39]

First: that no inclination of the heart toward this world remains, neither through desire nor through fear. Desire means that the heart is attached to one's family and children, to securing their welfare and warding off harm from them. Fear means being afraid of enemies and rivals. When God expands a person's breast, everything connected with this world becomes small in the eyes of his aspiration. It becomes like flies, gnats and mosquitoes, which neither desire draws him toward nor fear keeps him from. Everything becomes as nothing in his eyes, and then the heart turns entirely toward seeking the pleasure of God, the Exalted. In this analogy, the heart is like a spring of water, and human power, because of its weakness, is like a small spring. If you divide the water of one spring among many channels, its whole becomes weak. But when all of it pours into one place, it becomes strong. So Moses (peace be upon him) asked his Lord to expand his breast, by making him aware of the defects of this world and the ugliness of its qualities, until his heart became averse to it. Once that aversion was attained, it turned entirely toward the world of holiness and the stations of spiritual beings.

Second: when Moses (peace be upon him) was appointed to that great office, he needed heavy duties. Among them was preserving the revelation and persisting in the service of the Creator, glory be to Him. Among them also was the reform of the physical world. So he was, as it were, charged with managing two worlds, and turning toward one of them prevents occupation with the other. Do you not see that one occupied with sight is prevented from hearing, and one occupied with hearing is prevented from seeing and imagining? These faculties pull against one another and compete. Moses (peace be upon him) needed all of them. Whoever finds intimacy in the beauty of the Truth becomes estranged from the beauty of creation. So Moses asked his Lord to expand his breast by pouring upon him a perfection of power, so that his power would be sufficient to govern both worlds. This is what is meant by the expansion of the breast. The scholars gave examples for this meaning:

The first example: Know that the body as a whole is like a kingdom, the chest like a fortress, the heart like a palace, the inner heart (qalb) like a throne, the spirit like the king, the intellect like the vizier, desire like the great agent who brings blessings to the city, anger like the chief of police who is always occupied with striking and disciplining, the senses like spies, and the other faculties like servants, workers and craftsmen. Then Satan is an adversary to this city, this fortress and this king. Satan is the king, while passion, greed and the rest of the blameworthy traits are his soldiers. The spirit first sent out its vizier, which is the intellect. Likewise Satan sent out, in opposition to it, passion. So the intellect calls to God, the Exalted, while passion calls to Satan. Then the spirit sent out shrewdness to assist the intellect, and Satan sent out, in opposition to shrewdness, appetite. Shrewdness makes you aware of the defects of this world, while appetite moves you toward the pleasures of this world. Then the spirit supplied shrewdness with reflection, so that shrewdness would be strengthened by reflection, and it becomes aware of the present and absent defects, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "An hour of reflection is better than a year of worship." So Satan sent out heedlessness in opposition to reflection. Then the spirit sent out forbearance and steadfastness, for haste makes the good look ugly and the ugly look good, while forbearance makes the intellect aware of the ugliness of this world. So Satan sent out haste and rashness in opposition to it. For this reason the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Gentleness adorns anything it enters, and harshness disfigures anything it touches." For this reason God created the heavens and the earth in six days, so that gentleness and steadfastness might be learned from it. This is the conflict between the two groups, and your heart and breast are the fortress. Then this breast, which is the fortress, has a moat, which is asceticism in this world and lack of desire for it, and it has a wall, which is desire for the Hereafter and love of God, the Exalted. If the moat is deep and the wall is strong, Satan's army is unable to breach it, so they turn back and leave the fortress as it was. But if the moat of asceticism is not deep and the wall of love for the Hereafter is not strong, the adversary is able to seize the fortress of the breast. He enters it and his soldiers, namely passion, self-admiration, arrogance, miserliness, bad opinion of God, the Exalted, slander and backbiting, lodge in it. Then the king is confined to the palace and the matter becomes constricted for him. But when the aid of success comes and expels this army from the fortress, the matter is opened up, the breast is expanded, the darknesses of Satan depart, and the lights of the guidance of the Lord of the worlds enter. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾.

The second example: Know that the source of light is the heart. The occupation of a person with his wife and children, his desire to associate with people, and his fear of enemies form the veil that prevents the light of the sun of the heart from reaching the expanse of the breast. When God strengthens the insight of the servant until he perceives the helplessness of creatures and their lack of benefit in both abodes, they become small in his eyes. There is no doubt that, in themselves, they are pure nothingness, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾ [al-Qasas: 88]. So the servant continues to reflect on what is other than God, the Exalted, until he witnesses that they are pure nothingness. At that point the veil between his heart and the lights of the majesty of God, the Exalted, is removed. When the veil is removed, the heart is filled with light, and that is the expansion of the breast.

* * *

Chapter Six: On the breast. Know that the word is used while meaning the heart: ﴿Is one whose breast God has expanded for Islam [like one who is hardened]?﴾ [al-Zumar: 22]; ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾; ﴿and what is in the breasts is made known﴾ [al-ʿAdiyat: 10]; ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾ [Ghafir: 19]. It is also used while meaning the space in which the breast is: ﴿For indeed it is not the eyes that are blinded, but it is the hearts within the breasts that are blinded﴾ [al-Hajj: 46]. People differed over whether the seat of the intellect is the heart or the brain. The majority of the theologians hold that it is the heart. We have explained this issue in Surat al-Shuʿara in our commentary on His saying: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 193–194]. Some said: the terms are four, namely breast (sadr), heart (qalb), fu'ad and lubb (kernel of the intellect). The breast is the seat of Islam, as in: ﴿Is one whose breast God has expanded for Islam﴾ [al-Zumar: 22]. The heart is the seat of faith: ﴿But God has endeared faith to you and made it beautiful in your hearts﴾ [al-Hujurat: 7]. The fu'ad is the seat of knowledge: ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾ [al-Najm: 11]; ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the fu'ad, all of these will be questioned﴾ [al-Isra': 36]. The lubb is the seat of monotheism: ﴿Only people of intellect remember﴾ [al-Ra'd: 19].

Know that the heart, when it was first sent into this world, was sent blank of imprints, like a pure tablet. In the world of the body it is like the Preserved Tablet. Then God, may He be exalted, writes upon it with the pen of mercy and majesty everything connected with the world of intellect, such as the imprints of existing things and the forms of quiddities. This is like a single line that lasts until the end of the Resurrection for this lesser world. That is the abstract form and the purified state. Then the intellect rides the ship of success and casts it into the seas of the waves of intelligibles and the worlds of spiritual beings. From the winds of majesty and grandeur, the breeze of happiness sometimes blows, and at other times the west wind of misfortune. Sometimes the ship of contemplation reaches a shore radiant with majesty, and the lights of divinity shine upon it, and the intellect is freed from the darknesses of misguidance. Sometimes the ship plunges into the depths of ignorance, and it breaks and sinks. Wherever the ship is among the crashing waves of might, the guardian of the ship needs to seek lights and guidances, and there he says: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾.

Know that when the intellect begins to ascend from the lowest level of possibility to the height of necessity, its occupation with contemplating quiddities and its engagement with the abstract and the separate increases. It is known that every quiddity is either with it (the intellect) or belongs to it. If it is with it, the insight is filled with the lights of the majesty of divine might, and then no one remains there seeking to observe the rest of the lights, so everything other than Him, whether sight or insight, perishes. If the contemplation is directed toward what belongs to it, a wondrous state arises. It is like placing a pure crystal sphere so that the rays of the sun fall upon it, and those rays are reflected to a specific place, and that place to which the rays are reflected burns. Likewise, all possible quiddities are like pure crystal placed opposite the sun of holiness, the light of grandeur and the dawn of majesty. When the heart turns toward them, it acquires a relation to all of them together. Then the ray of divine greatness is reflected from each of them onto the heart, and the heart burns. It is known that the more numerous the things that burn, the more complete the burning. So he says: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾, until I become able to grasp the levels of possible things, and I reach the station of being burned by the lights of majesty. This is what is meant by the words of the Prophet (peace be upon him): "Show us things as they truly are." When he witnessed their burning by the lights of majesty, he said: "I cannot count the praise upon You."

[Page 40]

Chapter Seven: On the remaining discussions. He said: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾ and did not say "Expand my breast" in order to show that the benefit of that expansion returns to Moses (peace be upon him), not to God. As for the manner of the expansion of the breast of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the comparison between it and the expansion of the breast of Moses (peace be upon him), we will mention it, God willing, in the commentary on His saying: ﴿Did We not expand your breast for you?﴾ [al-Sharh: 1]. And God knows best what is correct.

* * *

The second requirement: His saying: ﴿And make my affair easy for me﴾. According to the People of the Sunnah, its meaning is the creation of ease. According to the Mu'tazilah, it means stirring the motives and incentives by performing facilitating favours (lutf, divine grace that makes obedience easier). If it is said: every favour that is possible has been done by God, the Exalted, so what is the benefit of this request? We say: it is possible that there are favours whose performance is fitting only after this request, so the benefit of the request is the fittingness of performing those favours.

The third requirement: His saying: ﴿And untie the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech﴾. It includes several issues.

The first issue: Know that speech is a great virtue, and this is shown by several considerations.

One of them: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He created man. He taught him eloquent speech﴾ [al-Rahman: 3–4]. He did not say "and taught him eloquence" with a conjunction, because if He had connected it with a conjunction, it would have been something different. But when the conjunction is omitted, His saying ﴿He taught him eloquent speech﴾ becomes like an explanation of His saying ﴿He created man﴾, as if He is only the Creator of man when He teaches him eloquent speech. This returns to the well-known statement that the quiddity of man is the rational speaking animal.

Second: the agreement of intelligent people on honouring the matter of the tongue. Zuhayr said:
"A man's tongue is half, and half is his heart; nothing remains but the form of flesh and blood."
ʿAlī said: "Without the tongue, a human being is only a neglected beast, or a shaped image." The meaning is that if we removed mental perception and verbal speech, nothing of the human would remain except the portion found in animals. They also said: "A man is his two smaller parts: his heart and his tongue." And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A person is hidden beneath his tongue."

Third: in the debate between Adam and the angels, virtue appeared only through speech, when He said: ﴿He said, "O Adam, inform them of their names." So when he informed them of their names, He said, "Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth?"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 33].

Fourthly: man is a substance composed of spirit and body. His spirit is from the world of the angels, so he constantly receives the forms of the unseen from the world of the angels. After that reception, he pours them out upon the world of bodies. His intermediary in the reception is discursive thought (al-fikr al-dhihni), and his intermediary in the outpouring is spoken utterance (al-nutq al-lisani). Just as that intermediary (thought) is among the greatest acts of worship, to the extent that it is said: "An hour of reflection is better than a year of worship," so the intermediary in conveying must be the most noble of the organs. Therefore His saying ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾ alludes to seeking the light that is situated in the spirit. His saying ﴿and ease my affair for me﴾ alludes to attaining that and facilitating that attainment. At that point, perfection in that spiritual reception is achieved. Nothing remains after this except the stage of expression (al-maqam al-bayani), which is pouring that perfection upon others, and that cannot happen except through the tongue. Hence He said: ﴿and loosen a knot from my tongue﴾.

Fifthly: knowledge is the most excellent of created things, as has been established, and generosity and giving are the most excellent acts of obedience. Among the organs, none is more excellent than the hand. Since the hand is the instrument of material giving, it was said: "The upper hand is better than the lower hand." Knowledge, which is better than wealth, has as its instrument of giving the tongue, so it must be the most noble of the organs. There is no doubt that the tongue is the instrument for giving knowledge, so it must be the most noble of the organs. Among people, however, there are those who praise silence, for several reasons:

[p. 42]

The first: His statement, peace be upon him: "Silence is wisdom, but few practise it." It is also related that a person's limbs admonish the tongue, saying: "Fear God regarding us, for if you go straight, we go straight, and if you go crooked, we go crooked."

The second: speech is of four kinds. Some of it has harm that is pure or predominant, some has harm and benefit equal, some has predominant benefit, and some is purely beneficial. As for that whose harm is pure or predominant, it must be abandoned. That in which both matters are equal is a fault. There remain the last two kinds, and separating them from the surplus of harm is difficult. Therefore, the better course is to refrain from speech.

The third: there is no existent or non-existent thing, creator or created, known or imagined, except that the tongue deals with it and addresses it by affirmation or negation. Whatever the mind (al-damir) conceives, the tongue expresses it, truly or falsely. This is a property not found in the other organs. The eye reaches only colours and forms, the ears reach only sounds and letters, and the hand reaches only bodies, and likewise the rest of the organs. The tongue, by contrast, has a vast field with no limit or boundary. It has broad scope for good and a deep sea for evil. It is light in cost and easy to acquire, unlike the other sins, which require many costly means that are mostly not easily obtained. Therefore, refraining from speech is the better course.

The fourth: they said: abstaining from speech has four names: ṣamt, sukūt, inṣāt, and iṣākha. As for ṣamt (silence), it is the most general, for it is used both for what is capable of speech and for what is not. For this reason one says: "wealth that speaks" (nāṭiq) and "wealth that is silent" (ṣāmit). As for sukūt, it is abstaining from speech by one who is able to speak. Inṣāt is silence together with listening, and whenever one of the two is separated from the other, it is not called inṣāt. He, exalted, said: ﴿So listen to it and be silent﴾ [al-A‘raf: 204]. Iṣākha is listening to what is difficult to perceive, such as a secret or a sound from a distant place.

Know that silence is an absence, and there is no virtue in it. Rather, speech in itself is a virtue, and vice lies in its misuse. Had it not been so, the interlocutor of God (Kalīm Allāh) would not have asked for this in His saying, exalted: ﴿and loosen a knot from my tongue﴾.

Second issue: they differed concerning the knot that was in the tongue of Moses, peace be upon him, on two views:

The first: that impediment was a creation of God, the Exalted, so he asked God, the Exalted, to remove it.

The second: its cause was that he, peace be upon him, during his childhood, took hold of Pharaoh's beard and plucked it. Pharaoh resolved to kill him and said: "This is the one through whose hand my kingdom will be lost." Āsiya said: "He is a child who does not understand. Test him: place a date and an ember before him." They placed them before him, and he took the ember and put it in his mouth. Scholars differed about this. Some said: neither the hand nor the tongue was burned, because the hand is the instrument of taking the staff, which is the proof, and the tongue is the instrument of remembrance (dhikr), so how could it burn? Also, Abraham, peace be upon him, was not burned by the fire of Nimrod, and Moses, peace be upon him, was not burned when he was cast into the oven, so how would he be burned here? Others said: the hand was burned but not the tongue, so that the right of eating together and sharing salt would not be lost.

The third: the tongue was burned but not the hand, because the boldness appeared through the hand, whereas the tongue had addressed Pharaoh with the words: "O father" (yā abatī).

The fourth: both were burned together, so that eating together and conversing would not be possible.

Third issue: they differed about why he, peace be upon him, asked for the loosening of that knot, on several grounds:

The first: so that no flaw whatsoever would occur in the performance of the message.

The second: to remove aversion, because a knot in the tongue may lead to contempt for its speaker and to people not paying attention to him.

The third: to show a miracle. Just as the restraint of the tongue of Zechariah, peace be upon him, from speech was a miracle for him, so too the release of the tongue of Moses, peace be upon him, is a miracle in his regard.

The fourth: seeking ease, for conveying such speech to someone like Pharaoh in his tyranny and arrogance is extremely difficult. When a knot in the tongue is added to that, the difficulty reaches its extreme. So he asked his Lord to remove that knot, as lightening and facilitation.

Fourth issue: al-Ḥasan, may God have mercy on him, said: that knot was entirely removed, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿You have been granted your request, O Moses﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 36]. This is weak, because he, peace be upon him, did not say: "Loosen the knot from my tongue" but rather said: ﴿loosen a knot from my tongue﴾. So if one knot is loosened, God has granted him his request. The truth is that most of the knots were loosened and a small amount remained, as His saying, quoted from Pharaoh: ﴿Am I not better than this one who is contemptible and can barely express himself?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 52]. That is, he almost cannot make himself clear. This indicates that he could express himself while some degree of impediment remained in his tongue. Two answers are given to this:

The first: what is meant by His saying ﴿and can barely express himself﴾ is that he does not bring any clear statement or proof.

The second: "kāda" here means "qaraba" (came near). Had the intended meaning been eloquence of the tongue, its sense would be that he does not come near to clarity, and that would be a complete negation of clarity. That is false, because he addressed Pharaoh and the assembly, and they understood his speech. How could clarity be negated entirely? Rather, Pharaoh said this only as a deception, to turn people's faces away from him. The people of allusion (ahl al-ishāra) said: He said ﴿loosen a knot from my tongue﴾ because the loosening of all knots is the portion of Muḥammad ﷺ. And He, exalted, said: ﴿and do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner﴾ [al-An‘am: 152]. Since that is the right of the orphan of Abū Ṭālib, indeed what revolves around it [is his]. And God knows best.

* * *

Fourth requirement: His saying: ﴿and appoint for me a vizier from my family﴾. Know that the request for a vizier is either because he feared his own inability to carry out that matter and so sought a helper, or because he saw that cooperation in religion and mutual support for it, together with sincere affection and the removal of suspicion, is a great merit in the matter of calling to God. For this reason Jesus, son of Mary, said: ﴿Who are my helpers toward God?﴾ The disciples said: ﴿We are God's helpers﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 14]. And He said to Muḥammad ﷺ: ﴿God is sufficient for you, and so are the believers who follow you﴾ [al-Anfal: 64]. And he, peace be upon him, said: "I have two viziers in heaven and two viziers on earth. The two in heaven are Gabriel and Michael, and the two on earth are Abū Bakr and ʿUmar." Here there are several issues:

First issue: the word vizier (wazīr) derives from wizr (burden), because he bears the king's burdens and loads, or from wazar, which is a mountain one takes refuge in, because the king relies on his opinion regarding his subjects and entrusts his affairs to him. Or it derives from muwāzara, which means assistance. Muwāzara is taken from the izār (waist-wrapper) of a man, which is the place a man tightens when he prepares to undertake a difficult task. This is what al-Aṣmaʿī said. The analogical form would have been ʾazīr, but the hamza was changed to a waw.

Second issue: he, peace be upon him, said: "When God desires good for a king, He provides him with a righteous vizier: if he forgets, the vizier reminds him; if he intends good, the vizier assists him; and if he intends evil, the vizier restrains him." Anūshirwān used to say: "The finest swords do not dispense with polishing, the most noble animals do not dispense with the whip, and the most knowledgeable kings do not dispense with a vizier."

Third issue: If it is said: seeking the help of a vizier is needed only by kings. As for the messenger charged with conveying the message and revelation from God, the Exalted, to a specific people, how does a vizier benefit him? Also, he, peace be upon him, asked his Lord to make him a partner in prophethood, saying: ﴿and make him a partner in my affair﴾. How then can he be a vizier?

The answer to the first: cooperation in the matter and mutual support for it, together with sincere affection and the removal of suspicion toward him, is a great merit in the effectiveness of calling to God, the Exalted. Moses, peace be upon him, was confident in his brother Aaron, so he asked his Lord to strengthen his back through him, so that he might bear, on their behalf, as much of the burden of conveyance as possible.

Fifth requirement: that this vizier be from his family, that is, from his relatives.

Sixth requirement: that the vizier from his family be his brother Aaron. He asked for this for two reasons:

The first: cooperation in religion is a great distinction, so he wanted this rank to be attained only by his own family. The second: each of them had the utmost love for the other and agreement with him. [p. 44] His saying ﴿Aaron﴾ has two possibilities in its grammatical position (intiṣāb):

The first: it is the object of the verb "make" (al-ja‘l), with the sense: "Make Aaron, my brother, a vizier for me."

The second: it is in apposition (badal) to "vizier," and "my brother" is an attribute (naʿt) of Aaron or an apposition.

Know that Aaron, peace be upon him, was distinguished by several qualities. Among them: eloquence, as He said of Moses: ﴿And my brother Aaron is more eloquent than I in speech﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 34]. Among them: gentleness, for He said: ﴿He said: O son of my mother, do not seize my beard or my head﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 94]. And among them: he was older than Moses in age.

Seventh requirement: His saying: ﴿strengthen my back through him﴾. On this there are several issues:

First issue: The common reading is "ushdud bihi wa ashrikhu" (strengthen through him and make him a partner) as supplication. Ibn ʿĀmir alone read "ashdid wa ashrikhu" in the form of a conditional answer, as a report from Moses, peace be upon him, meaning: "I will do that." For one who reads it in the imperative form, it is permissible to make "my brother" nominative as the subject (mubtadaʾ), with "ushdud bihi" as its predicate, and to pause at "Aaron."

Second issue: al-azr means strength, and āzarahu means "he strengthened him." God, the Exalted, said: ﴿so he strengthened it﴾ [al-Fath: 29], meaning he helped it. Abū ʿUbayda said: "azrī" means my back. In the Book of al-Khalīl: al-azr is the back.

Third issue: when he, peace be upon him, asked God, the Exalted, to make Aaron his vizier, he asked Him also to strengthen his back through him and to make him a helper, because there is no reliance on kinship alone.

The eighth matter: His saying, ﴿And associate him in my affair﴾. "The affair" here refers to prophethood. He said this because he (peace be upon him) knew that he would strengthen his arm (ya shuddu bihi ʿadudahu) through him, and he was older than him in years and more eloquent in tongue. Then, Glorified and Exalted is He, related about the two of them that, for its sake, they supplicated with this supplication, saying: ﴿That we may glorify You much﴾ and ﴿remember You much﴾. Tasbih (glorification) may be understood as being by the tongue and by belief. In either case, tasbih is declaring Allah Exalted free of His essence, His attributes and His actions, of whatever is not befitting to Him. As for dhikr (remembrance), it is describing Allah Exalted with the attributes of majesty and greatness. There is no doubt that negation precedes affirmation. As for His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Indeed You are ever Seeing of us﴾, there are several interpretations (wujuh):

First: You know that we do not intend by these acts of obedience except Your face and Your pleasure, and we do not intend by them anyone other than You.

Second: ﴿You have been Seeing of us﴾, because this seeking of help through these things is for the sake of my need for them in prophethood.

Third: You are Seeing of the aspects of our interests, so give us what is most beneficial for us. He restricted the supplication with this (phrase) out of reverence for his Lord, lest He be subject to his command, and as a complete entrusting of the matter to Him.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 20, verses 25–35 (part 1 of 7):**

[Page 28]

**Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He said, "My Lord, expand for me my breast. And ease for me my task. And untie the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech. And appoint for me a helper from my family, Aaron, my brother. Strengthen through him my back, and let him share in my task, that we may glorify You much and remember You much. Indeed You are ever Seeing of us."﴾**

Know that when Allah the Exalted commanded Moses (peace be upon him) to go to Pharaoh, and that was a difficult obligation (taklif shaqq), he therefore asked his Lord for eight matters, then concluded them with what serves as the reason (‘illah) for asking those things.

The first matter: His saying, ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾. Know that it is said, "I explained (sharahtu) the speech," meaning I clarified it, and "I expanded (sharahtu) his breast," meaning I widened it. The first meaning is close to the second, because the explanation of speech is only achieved by spreading it out. The reason for this request is what Allah the Exalted related of him in another place, His saying: ﴿And my breast tightens and my tongue does not speak freely﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 13]. So he asked Allah the Exalted to replace that tightness with expansiveness, and said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, so that I may understand from You what You have revealed to me. It was also said: [he asked You to] encourage me, so that I may be bold enough to address Pharaoh.

Then the discussion regarding this involves several matters:

First: the benefit of supplication and its conditions.
Second: the reason why a person, at the time of supplication, mentions none of Allah's names except "the Lord" (al-Rabb).
Third: what is the meaning of expanding the breast.
Fourth: by what means the breast is expanded.
Fifth: how the expansion of the breast occurred for Moses (peace be upon him) and for Muhammad (ﷺ).
Sixth: the state of Moses' breast (peace be upon him): was it already expanded or was it not? If it was already expanded, then asking for its expansion would be seeking to obtain what is already obtained (tahsil al-hasil), which is impossible. And if it was not expanded, then that is false for two reasons:

The first: that He (glorified is He) had already made clear to him, in what preceded, everything related to the religions, including knowledge of divinity (rububiyyah) and servitude (ubudiyyah) and the states of the return (al-ma'ad). Everything related to the expansion of the breast in matters of religion had therefore been achieved. Then He (glorified is He) showed him kindness with His saying: ﴿And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed﴾, then addressed him gently with His saying: ﴿And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?﴾. Then He showed him great miracles and noble honors, then gave him the station of messengership after he had been poor. Everything related to honor and dignity had been achieved for him. Even if a single particle of these stations had been attained by the lowest of people, he would have become one whose breast is expanded. So after these had been attained by the one whom Allah the Exalted spoke to directly (Kalim Allah), it is impossible that his breast would not be expanded.

The second: that since his breast had not become expanded after these things, it would not be permissible for Allah the Exalted to entrust prophethood to him, for one whose heart is tight and whose mind is troubled is not fit for judgment. As he (peace be upon him) said: "A judge should not judge while he is angry." How then can one be fit for prophethood, the lowest rank of which is judgment?

These are the combined matters that must be investigated concerning this verse.

As for the first investigation, namely the benefit of supplication and its conditions, it has already been addressed in the explanation of His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286]. However, we will mention here some benefits related to this place. So we say: know that perfection has levels and degrees, and the highest of them is that a thing is perfect in its essence and perfects others. As for its being perfect in its essence, whatever is such has its perfection as a necessary part of its essence, and whatever is such was perfect from eternity. But it is impossible for it to be perfecting from eternity, because perfecting (takmil) means making a thing perfect, and that is not realized except when perfection is absent. For if it were already present from eternity, influence on it would be impossible, since obtaining what is already obtained is impossible, and bringing into being what already exists is impossible. Therefore He (glorified is He), although perfect from eternity, becomes a perfecter in what is continually renewed.

If it is said: since perfecting is one of the attributes of perfection, then when He was not a perfecter from eternity, He was devoid of the attributes of perfection, and so He would be deficient, which is impossible. We answer: deficiency would only follow if that were possible from eternity. We have explained that an eternal act is impossible, so eternal perfecting is impossible, and its absence is therefore not a deficiency. Just as our saying that He is not able to create the like of His own essence is not a deficiency, because that is not possible in itself. And like our saying that He does not know a detailed number of the movements of the people of Paradise, because whatever has a detailed number is finite, and the movements of the people of Paradise are infinite, so it has no detailed number. This is impossible not because of a deficiency in His knowledge, but because it is impossible in its own nature to occur.

Having established this, we say: when He (glorified is He) intended to bring into being, and the purpose of that was to perfect the deficient, because possible things are receptive to existence, and the attribute of existence is an attribute of perfection, then His power over perfecting required setting up a table of perfection for possible things. So He seated upon the table some of the non-existent things and not others, for several reasons:

First: non-existent things are infinite, so if He had seated all of them at the table of existence, what has no end would have entered existence.

Second: if He had brought all of them into being, He would not remain after that able to bring things into being, because bringing into being what already exists is impossible. That would, although it is a perfection for the deficient, entail the deficiency of the Perfect, for the Capable would turn from capacity to incapacity.

Third: if all had entered existence, no distinction would remain in it, so the one who chooses would not be distinguished from the one who is compelled by nature. Power is a perfection, and acting by nature is a deficiency. For these reasons He brought some of the possible things out into existence.

If it is said that two objections arise against this:

One: that existent things are finite and non-existent things are infinite, and there is no ratio of the finite to the infinite. So then the hospitality would be hospitality for the lesser. As for deprivation, it is a count of what has no end, and this would not be existence.

Two: if the portion He singled out for this hospitality was singled out because of a worthiness that arose in it and not in others, then from whom did that worthiness arise? And if it was not for this worthiness, then that would be futile, and futility is impossible, as it has been said:

*He gives and withholds, not out of stinginess nor out of generosity.*

And it is not fitting for the Most Generous of the generous. The answer to all of this is that these doubts only revolve in minds and imaginations, because a person tries to measure His act by our act, and that is false, since He is not questioned about what He does, but they are questioned.

Having understood this, this existence overflowing from the light of His mercy upon all possible things is the general hospitality and the all-encompassing table, and it is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And My mercy encompasses all things﴾ [al-A'raf: 156]. Then existent things divided into inanimate things (jamadat) and living beings (hayawanat). There is no doubt that the inanimate, in relation to the living, is like non-existence in relation to existence, because the inanimate has no awareness of its own existence, so its existence in relation to it is like non-existence, and its non-existence is like existence. As for the living, it is the one who distinguishes between the existent and the non-existent, and these two differ in relation to it. Also, the inanimate in relation to the living is an instrument, because living beings use inanimate things for the purposes and interests of themselves, and they are like an obedient, subjugated servant, while the living being is like a sovereign owner. So being alive is better than being inanimate. Just as the kindness and mercy of Allah required setting up the table of existence for some non-existent things and not others, likewise they required setting up the table of life for some existent things and not others. Therefore He made some existent things living and not others.

Life, in relation to inanimacy, is like light in relation to darkness, sight in relation to blindness, and existence in relation to non-existence. At that point some existent things became living, perceiving what is contrary and what is agreeable, pleasure and pain, good and evil. Hence the living beings said at that moment: "O Lord of lords, although we have found the robe of existence and the robe of life, and You have honored us with that, yet our need has increased. For in the state of non-existence and inanimacy we did not need what is agreeable and suitable, and we did not fear what is contrary and harmful. But when existence and life were obtained, we came to need seeking what is agreeable and repelling what is contrary. If we have no power to flee, to seek, to repel, and to draw near, we will remain like a paralyzed person on the road, exposed to calamities and a target for the arrows of afflictions. So give us, from the treasuries of Your mercy, the power and strength by which we may be able to seek at one time and flee at another." Thus complete mercy required the specification of some living beings with power, just as it required the specification of some existent things with life and the specification of some non-existent things with existence.

Then those who have power said at that point: "Our God, the Generous, the Bountiful, life and power without intellect exist only in one of two categories: either for the madmen bound with chains and shackles, or for the beasts used for carrying loads, and all of that is among the attributes of deficiency. You have raised us from the abyss of deficiency to the summit of perfection. So bestow upon us from the intellect, which is the noblest of Your creatures and the most excellent of Your originations, the one You honored by Your saying: 'By You I humble, by You I reward, and by You I punish,' so that we may succeed, from the treasuries of Your mercy, with complete robes and perfect excellence." So He gave them intellect and sent into their spirits the light of insight and the essence of guidance.

[Page 30]

At this level they attained the four robes: existence, life, power, and intellect.

Intellect is the seal of all of them, and the seal must be the most excellent. Do you not see that when our Messenger (ﷺ) was the Seal of the Prophets, he was the most excellent of the prophets (upon them be blessings and peace)? And when man was the seal of corporeal creatures, he was the most excellent of them. Likewise, when intellect was the seal of the robes flowing from the presence of the Lord of Majesty, it was the most excellent and most perfect of the robes. Then intellect looked into itself and saw itself like a bowl full of precious jewels, or rather like a sky full of shining stars, which are the self-evident necessary knowledges (al-'ulum al-darurriyyah al-badihiyyah) fixed in the primary beginnings of minds and the pure intellects. Just as the stars fixed in the heavens are signs by which one is guided in the darknesses of land and sea, so too the jewels fixed in the sky of intellect are shining stars by which travelers are guided in the darknesses of the world of bodies toward the lights of the spiritual world and the expanse of the heavens and their radiances.

When intellect looked at those shining stars and dazzling jewels, it saw the mark of createdness (ruqm al-huduth) upon those jewels and upon all those robes. So it inferred from those marks a marker, and from those engravings an engraver. At that point it knew that the engraver is other than the engraving, and the builder is other than the building. Thus there opened for it, from the highest sky of the world of created things, openings toward the lights of the shining signs of the world of eternity (qidam). It gazed upon the world of eternity, the eternal and majestic. Yet intellect had only looked at the lights of the world of eternity from the darknesses of the world of createdness and contingency, so the astonishment of the lights of eternity overwhelmed it, its eyes were blinded, and it remained bewildered. So it turned by its nature to the Bestower of lights and said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾. For the seas are deep, the darknesses are dense, there are highwaymen of enemies, both internal and external, and the devils of humans and jinn are many. If You do not expand my breast and are not a help to me in all matters, these robes will be cut off and become a cause of reaching calamities, not of attaining the ranks. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾.

* * *

[Page 31]

Then he said: ﴿And ease my task for me﴾. This is because everything that proceeds from the servant, whether actions, speech, movements or stillnesses, cannot come into being unless the servant first becomes willing to do it. This willingness (*irada*) is an originated attribute, and it necessarily requires an agent. If the agent of this willingness is the servant himself, then bringing about that willingness would require yet another willingness, and this leads to an infinite regress (*tasalsul*). Rather, one must arrive at a willingness that is created by the Administrator of the world, so that He is in reality the One who eases affairs and the One who completes all things. The complete verification is that the occurrence of an attribute necessarily requires a receptive recipient (*qabil*) and an agent (*fa'il*). Thus he expressed the readiness of the recipient by his saying: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾, and he expressed the attainment of the agent by his saying: ﴿And ease my task for me﴾. In this there is an indication that He, glorified and exalted, is the One who gives the recipient its receptivity and the agent its agency. For this reason, the early generations (*al-salaf*), may Allah be pleased with them, used to say: "O You who bestow favours before they are deserved."

The combination of these two statements is like a decisive proof that all events in this world occur by His decree, His destiny, His wisdom and His power.

It is also possible to say: as if Moses, peace be upon him, said: "My God, I am not content with the expansion of the breast, but I ask You to carry out the matter and to achieve the aim." Therefore he said: ﴿And ease my task for me﴾.

Or it may be said: when He, glorified and exalted, bestowed upon him the four robes of honour (*khil'a*), namely existence, life, power and intellect, it was as if He said to him: "O Moses, I have given you these four robes of honour, so there must be, in return for them, four services, so that every blessing is met with a service." Moses, peace be upon him, said: "What are those services?" He said: ﴿And establish the prayer for My remembrance﴾. For in it there are four kinds of service: standing, recitation, bowing and prostration. So when you perform the prayer, you have met every blessing with a service.

Then, when He, exalted, bestowed upon him the fifth robe of honour, which is the robe of prophethood, he said: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾, so that I may know with what service I should meet this blessing. It was said to him that he should strive in fulfilling this message in the required manner. Moses said: "My Lord, this cannot be accomplished by me, given my weakness, my feebleness, the scarcity of my instruments and the strength of my adversary. So expand my breast for me and ease my task for me."

* * *

[Page 32]

**The second section: on His saying: ﴿My Lord, expand my breast for me﴾.**

Know that supplication (*du'a'*) is a means of nearness to Allah, exalted. Moses occupied himself with this supplication seeking nearness. This requires the demonstration of two matters: first, showing that supplication is a means of nearness; second, showing that Moses, peace be upon him, sought nearness through this supplication.

As for showing that supplication is a means of nearness, several considerations indicate it:

The first: Allah, exalted, has mentioned questions and answers in His Book in a number of places, some concerning fundamentals (*usuliyya*) and some concerning rulings (*furu'iyya*). As for the fundamental ones, the first is in al-Baqarah: ﴿They ask you about the crescent moons. Say: they are times set for people and for the pilgrimage﴾ [al-Baqarah: 189].

The second, concerning the Children of Israel: ﴿They ask you about the spirit. Say: the spirit is of the command of my Lord﴾ [al-Isra': 85].

The third: ﴿They ask you about the mountains. Say: my Lord will scatter them as dust﴾ [Ta-Ha: 105].

The fourth: ﴿They ask you about the Hour, when it will come to pass﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 42].

As for the ruling-related ones, there are six in al-Baqarah in sequence:

One: ﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: whatever good you spend is for parents and relatives﴾ [al-Baqarah: 215].

Two: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: fighting in it is a great matter﴾ [al-Baqarah: 217].

Three: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: in both there is great sin﴾ [al-Baqarah: 219].

Four: ﴿And they ask you what they should spend. Say: the surplus﴾ [al-Baqarah: 219].

Five: ﴿And they ask you about orphans. Say: setting things right for them is good﴾ [al-Baqarah: 220].

Six: ﴿And they ask you about menstruation. Say: it is an affliction﴾ [al-Baqarah: 222].

Seven: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: the spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾ [al-Anfal: 1].

Eight: ﴿And they ask you about Dhu'l-Qarnayn. Say: I will recite to you a mention of him﴾ [al-Kahf: 83].

Nine: ﴿And they ask you to inform them: is it true? Say: yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true﴾ [Yunus: 53].

Ten: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the one who leaves no heir (*kalala*)﴾ [al-Nisa': 176].

Eleven: ﴿And when My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near﴾ [al-Baqarah: 186].

Having known this, we say: these questions and answers came in different forms. Most commonly, when He mentioned a question, He said to Muhammad ﷺ: "Say" (*qul*). In another form the answer came with the phrase "so say" (*faqul*) with the particle of consequence (*fa*, of sequence). In a third form, He mentioned the question without mentioning the answer, as in His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour, when it will come to pass﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 42]. In a fourth form, He mentioned the answer without using the word "say" or "so say", as in His saying: ﴿And when My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near﴾ [al-Baqarah: 186]. These things must have a benefit, so we say:

As for answers introduced by the word "say", there is no difficulty with them, because His saying "say" is like a fixed seal confirming the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, and like a fixed honour in that he is addressed by Allah, exalted, with conveying the revelation and delivering the message.

As for the second form, His saying: ﴿So say: my Lord will scatter them as dust﴾ [Ta-Ha: 105], the reason is that their saying ﴿They ask you about the mountains﴾ [Ta-Ha: 105] is a question either about their pre-eternity or about the necessity of their continuance. This matter is among the foundational issues of the religion. Therefore Allah, exalted, commanded Muhammad ﷺ to answer with the particle *fa*, which indicates immediate sequence, as if He, glorified, said: "O Muhammad, answer this question right away and do not delay, for doubt concerning it is disbelief, and do not postpone this matter lest they fall into doubt and confusion." Then the manner of the answer was: ﴿So say: my Lord will scatter them as dust﴾. There is no doubt that scattering is possible, because it is possible for every part of the mountain, and the senses confirm this. It must therefore be possible for the whole mountain. This indicates that it is not eternal nor necessarily existent, because the eternal does not admit change or scattering.

If it is said: they said, "Tell us about your God: is He gold, silver or iron?" and He said: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 1], without saying "so say: He is Allah, the One", even though this matter is of great importance. We reply: He, exalted, did not relate their question in this place, and the particle *fa* is a conjunctive particle which requires a preceding statement. When this was absent, He omitted the *fa*. Unlike here, where He related their question, so it was fitting to connect the answer to it with the particle *fa*.

As for the third form: He, exalted, did not mention the answer in His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour, when it will come to pass﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 42]. The wisdom in this is that knowing the time of the Hour precisely involves the corruptions that we explained earlier. For this reason Allah, exalted, did not mention that answer. This indicates that among questions there are some that are not answered.

As for the fourth form: His saying ﴿indeed I am near﴾, without mentioning "say" in its answer. There are several considerations here:

The first: this indicates the exaltation of the status of supplication, and that it is among the greatest acts of worship. As if He, glorified, said: "O My servant, you need an intermediary in other matters, but in the station of supplication there is no intermediary between Me and you." This is shown by the fact that every story that was narrated was not important to know, and He said to His Messenger ﷺ: "Recount to them that story," as in His saying: ﴿And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 27]; ﴿And recite to them the story of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he withdrew from them﴾ [al-A'raf: 175]; ﴿And mention in the Book Moses﴾ [Maryam: 51]; ﴿And mention in the Book Isma'il﴾ [Maryam: 54]; ﴿And mention in the Book Idris﴾ [Maryam: 56]; ﴿And inform them about the guests of Abraham﴾ [al-Hijr: 51].
